title: Cardinal Billing Account Rules Manual: Late Fee Conditions, Grace Days and Courtesy Waivers
content:
## Section 3. Late fees on the Cardinal Billing Account

3.1 **Former charging clause (retired).** The clause stating that a late fee of the plan's late fee is charged once on an installment that is still unpaid, beyond the underpayment tolerance, at the end of the plan's grace days after its due date, is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current late fee charge basis.

3.2 **When no late fee is charged.** No late fee is charged:
- on the down payment of a new-business term;
- on a final earned-premium bill;
- on an account in notice pending, cancelled for nonpayment, collections or closed status;
- once the pay plan's maximum number of late fees per term has been charged in the term (counting the late fees charged in the current policy term).

3.3 **Grace days.** A late fee is charged only when the installment is still unpaid after the pay plan's late fee grace days (calendar days) past its due date. The count starts the day after the due date of the installment invoice, so the fee can post on the first day after the last grace day and never on a grace day. The due date is read from the installment's invoice on the account's billing history, before the fee is charged.

3.4 **Courtesy waiver.** A late fee may be waived as a courtesy on the customer's request when the account has used fewer than the pay plan's courtesy late fee waivers per 12 months in the rolling 12 months (counting courtesy waivers on the account in the 12 calendar months ending on the waiver date) and the installment it was charged on has since been paid in full. Whether a given late fee has already been waived is read from the account's billing history for that fee.

3.5 **Posting error.** A late fee charged in error (the payment had posted on or before the end of the grace days) is always reversed, with the waiver reason "posting error".

3.6 **Plan figures used.** The late fee, the grace days and the per-term cap are each the figure of the account's own pay plan, for every one of the six pay plans.

## Grace count, shown on both sides (abstract days)

Take an installment due on day D on a plan with 5 grace days.

| Day | Status of the day | May a late fee post? |
|---|---|---|
| D | Due date | No |
| D plus 1 through D plus 5 | Grace days | No, never on a grace day |
| D plus 6 | First day after the last grace day | Yes, if the installment is still unpaid |

On a plan with 3 grace days the first day a fee may post is D plus 4; with 7 grace days, D plus 8.

## Courtesy waiver points of judgement (hypothetical)

| Courtesy waivers used in the rolling 12 months | Plan allowance | Installment since paid in full | Courtesy waiver available |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | Yes | Yes |
| 1 | 1 | Yes | No, not fewer than the allowance |
| 0 | 1 | No | No |
| 0 | 0 | Yes | No, not fewer than the allowance |

A fee reversed for a posting error is a separate rule (3.5): it is reversed whatever the courtesy waiver count.

superseded_clauses: A late fee of the plan's late_fee is charged once on an installment that is still unpaid, beyond the underpayment_tolerance, at the end of late_fee_grace_days calendar days after its due date.
